title: Review-feedback capture — plan 001
epic_title: Build the review-feedback ledger — the operator-conversation capture slice

tasks.title: Build the review-feedback ledger storage class and its fold
tasks.goal: a per-subject append-only ledger entry can be written to disk and a fold produces a byte-verified machine projection.
tasks.current: no ledger exists; human review comments are discarded.
tasks.desired: a per-subject directory holds one append-only markdown file per entry (id · source · author · timestamp · subject-anchor · verbatim comment); a fold reads all entries and regenerates a schema-versioned projection; the projection is byte-verified (a stale/hand-edited projection reds the gate); an entry file is append-only (capture writes the initial block, a later disposition transition appends, prior content never rewritten).
scope: the entry schema (typed, append-only) and the per-subject directory layout
the fold that produces the machine projection, wired as a docgate verb + byte-verify
acceptance: writing N entries under a subject yields N append-only files, each with all header fields populated
the fold regenerates the projection deterministically; a byte-mismatch reds `verify-generated`
appending a disposition transition to an entry leaves its captured text and attribution unchanged
key_interfaces: the ledger `Entry` schema-versioned type; the fold entry point; the projection contract

tasks.title: Introduce the CaptureSource port and the coded writer
tasks.goal: the coded writer produces a ledger entry from a captured comment, taken through the consumer-side CaptureSource port.
tasks.current: T1 can persist an entry, but nothing produces one from a review comment.
tasks.desired: a consumer-side `CaptureSource` interface yields a schema-versioned captured comment (comment · author · timestamp · subject-anchor · source-id); the writer is the sole producer of entries (no hand-authoring path) and imports no adapter package (boundary lint-enforced). *(Plan decision: the port is built now — the frozen design's DINV-2 binds it, and the WR-4 code-host adapter forward-composes on it; the conversation adapter is live in this slice, added in T3.)*
scope: the `CaptureSource` interface and the writer, with a test/stub adapter for the conformance suite
the import-boundary lint that keeps the writer core adapter-free
acceptance: the writer produces one entry per captured comment via the port, verified with a stub adapter
the import-boundary lint fails if the writer core imports an adapter package
no code path or guide permits hand-authoring an entry

tasks.title: Capture operator-conversation comments through the port
tasks.goal: explicitly capturing an operator-conversation comment persists it as a ledger entry without coupling capture to the source edit.
tasks.current: operator-conversation comments can cause source edits, but the comments are not automatically persisted.
tasks.desired: an explicit capture command uses the conversation adapter to record the selected comment as a ledger entry. Capture stays independent from editing: a failed write reports the failure and leaves the supplied comment available for retry, while source edits remain governed by the operator conversation.
scope: the conversation adapter implementing `CaptureSource`; the explicit capture command and retry-safe failure behavior
out_of_scope: disposition (T4); operator-conversation editing behavior itself (NR-1, guarded in T8)
acceptance: an explicitly captured conversation comment produces one entry with all fields; source editing remains independent
a simulated write failure loses no comment and blocks no review (UB-1)
the command contains no capture logic beyond parsing input and invoking the adapter and writer
key_interfaces: the conversation adapter (implements `CaptureSource`); the explicit capture-command contract

tasks.title: Tag dispositions at resolution (conversation side)
tasks.goal: an entry closes to a typed disposition + outcome-ref when its resolving event is observed — deterministically, never by inference.
tasks.current: entries are captured open, with no disposition.
tasks.desired: the writer records the edit-commit an annotation produced at capture; the fold observes that commit's landing on the subject and tags the entry `applied` with a stable outcome-ref (merged sha / PR / amendment id — never a working-branch sha); an entry whose annotation produced no landed change closes `no-action` with a reason; one not yet resolvable stays open, flagged pending; one whose subject anchor no longer resolves is retained, flagged stale. Every disposition transition names the observed event it was set from.
scope: the disposition state machine; the deterministic resolving-event (commit-landing) observation; and the pending, no-action, and stale-subject handling
acceptance: a landed annotation-edit closes its entry `applied` with a stable outcome-ref naming the observed commit
a no-change subject closes `no-action`; an unresolved one stays pending; a superseded-or-deleted subject stays flagged-stale (UB-3, UB-5, UB-6)
every disposition transition cites its resolving event; no code path sets a disposition without one
key_interfaces: the disposition enum + transition; the resolving-event observer; the outcome-ref shape

tasks.title: The review-feedback citation grammar and its enforced resolution check
tasks.goal: an entry resolves by its `review-feedback:` citation, and a dead citation or outcome-ref reds the gate.
tasks.current: `Learned-from: review-thread` refs resolve to nothing; nothing enforces resolution.
tasks.desired: entries carry a `review-feedback:<subject-stem>#<entry-anchor>` citation (a sibling of the existing grammar, grep-resolvable); `Learned-from: review-thread` resolves to a `review-feedback:` anchor through the amendment model's existing free ref slot (no amendment-model change); a registry-born docgate check (extending the check-registration pattern) fails any entry `outcome` ref or `Learned-from: review-thread` ref that does not resolve.
scope: the `review-feedback:` citation family; the registry-born resolution check
out_of_scope: any change to the amendment model (its free ref slot is used as-is); cross-links (T6)
acceptance: a `review-feedback:` citation resolves by grep to its entry; a dead ref reds the resolution check
a `Learned-from: review-thread` ref pointing at a real entry passes; a dangling one reds the check
the amendment-model files are unchanged by this task
key_interfaces: the `review-feedback:` anchor grammar; the resolution check registration

tasks.title: Cross-link entries to the existing captures, read-only
tasks.goal: an entry cross-links to a reviewer M2 residual or an Argus `E-n` disposition, one-directionally.
tasks.current: no linkage between the ledger and the existing partial captures.
tasks.desired: an entry may cite the reviewer M2 report / Argus `E-n` where relevant; the links are one-directional (we cite them; `review-report/v1` and the Argus ledgers are never edited to cite back).
scope: the one-directional cross-link citations from an entry
out_of_scope: any write to `review-report/v1` or the Argus ledgers (NG-5)
acceptance: an entry's cross-link resolves to its target; the target files are unmodified

tasks.title: Compute the ledger-native measures in the fold
tasks.goal: the fold exposes disposition counts, the applied-vs-decline ratio, and `edit_distance` — all from the ledger alone.
tasks.desired: the fold's projection exposes disposition counts per type, the applied-vs-decline ratio over disposed entries, and an `edit_distance` frozen in each `applied` entry at write time (computed when the writer tags the outcome — no later diff read); all read by inspecting the projection (the event stream is deferred, WR-6).
scope: the measure computations in the fold; `edit_distance` capture at disposition-write
out_of_scope: the all-proposals rejection rate (optimizer's, NG-1); a consumer reading the measures (WR-5)
acceptance: disposition counts + applied-vs-decline ratio + `edit_distance` compute from the projection alone, for a subject class
`edit_distance` is frozen in the entry at disposition-write, not recomputed on read
key_interfaces: the measures block of the projection; the `edit_distance` field

tasks.title: Guard the non-regressions
tasks.goal: the change is provably additive — operator-conversation review, the reviewers' posture, the merge path, and the existing captures are untouched.
tasks.current: these behaviors exist and pass their suites today.
tasks.desired: operator-conversation editing remains independent from capture (NR-1); no pipeline path acquires a required human-review step (NR-2); merge authorization / required checks / risk lanes are unchanged (NR-3); `review-report/v1` and the Argus ledgers are unchanged (NR-4).
scope: regression tests / inspections asserting each non-regression holds
out_of_scope: none — this task only verifies, it changes no behavior
acceptance: the existing conversation-capture, reviewer, and merge-path suites pass
no diff touches `review-report/v1`, the Argus ledgers, or the merge-path config
